newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Wreck of QE ocean liner to rest under HK port.
newsitem.headline: Wreck of QE ocean liner to rest under HK port.

text.p: The once-proud luxury ocean liner Queen Elizabeth, which sank in a mysterious blaze in Hong Kong 25 years ago, will be given a final resting place under the colony's new container port, a port official said on Saturday.

Container Terminal Nine will be built on reclaimed land extending over wreckage from the 83,000 tonne liner, which was bought by Tung Chao-yung, the father of Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa, from the Cunard shipping group in 1970.
"It is too expensive to salvage the ship wreckage, which is deep, covered in mud. And it poses no danger to shipping in the area," Port Development Board secretary Richard Yuen said by telephone.
Police have never caught the arsonists who torched the ship off Tsing Yi Island on January 9, 1972. The fire was officially attributed to sabotage.

Flamboyant Hong Kong shipping magnate C.Y. Tung had planned to turn the cruise ship, which once recorded the fastest sea crossing of the Atlantic Ocean, into a HK$30 million ($3.8 million) floating university.
C.Y. Tung's son takes over as leader of Hong Kong when the territory reverts to Chinese rule on July 1.
